source.title: Visual Fairness Misalignment: AI Models Prefer People Based on How They Look
source.authors: Mostufa Jbareen; Amit LeVi; Rom Himelstein; Avi Mendelson; Brit Youngmann

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text includes the main paper and supplementary material.
record.tranche_reason: The study estimates a harmful-minus-harmless activation direction and intervenes on it to reduce refusals, reporting answer rates. It adapts the method to multimodal VLM inputs and does not report the original all-layer-and-position ablation as a separate intervention.
record.gate_note: The study reports refusal-direction steering success rates and answer consistency. The cosine-similarity plots are not refusal-rate outcomes, and the layer/strength calibration values are choices for the intervention, so they are not separate result rows. The paper compares other elicitation methods, but their results are not rows for the direction-based intervention. It reports no direction addition, weight edit, general-capability evaluation, or cross-language/base-to-instruct transfer test. It says Qwen3-VL and DeepSeek-VL2 had no refusals, but does not give their V-SBB ASR values in Table 1.
record.test_reason: The study applies Arditi-style difference-in-means refusal-direction intervention to a new setting: vision-language models on image-based demographic selection queries. It reports refusal-suppression rates (ASR) against unsteered baselines, which bears on V1's removal claim. Its main aim is bias measurement, but the ASR-vs-clean numbers are a direct result on whether removing the direction removes refusal. This is a new setting rather than the same method and measure, so T3 fits better than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that multimodal refusal steering reduces refusals more than cipher-text or text-only SBB baselines while preserving models' original selections. They say this exposes visual demographic preferences hidden by safety alignment, and that these preferences vary widely across VLMs and persist on real images. Note that measured answer consistency is only 45.9–88.2%, so 'largely preserving' is the authors' framing rather than uniform.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-minus-harmless mean activations and activation-space refusal steering, but adapts direction extraction to paired text-image inputs and selects a single intervention layer. The reported results do not isolate all-layer/all-position ablation from direction subtraction.
record.method_sensitivity: The intervention layer is chosen per model as the layer with the largest refusal-rate reduction; intervention strength is calibrated per model and direction. The study uses five random-seed directions and counts a query as successful if at least one produces a valid answer.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal-direction steering changes the selected answer on many queries the model already answered unsteered. Answer consistency is 45.9% for Llama-3.2-Vision and roughly 57–88% for the other models, against about 100% for clean re-runs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-direction removal alters non-refusal outputs on the same inputs (side effects beyond refusal).

record.peer_reviewed: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026), Workshop: TAE (Trust-AI-Eval): Can We Trust AI Evaluation?
record.problems: Table 1 reports ASR for only three of the six evaluated models; the text says two other models had no refusals but does not provide their V-SBB ASR values there. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Answer consistency applies only to queries answered without intervention and is not a general-capability test. The reported steering results do not separately identify subtraction versus ablation.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-version results were reported. The paper’s demographic preference distributions and cosine-similarity plots were not cataloged as rows because they do not directly measure the refusal behavior or general capabilities named by the tested version; the cosine plots are figure-based and the paper uses them in describing direction alignment and intervention-layer selection.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; all-layer, all-position ablation; preservation of general capabilities; harmful-instruction refusal benchmarks (only demographic-selection queries are tested).
All: text-only to multimodal non-transfer is cited from Liu et al., not tested here.

missing.what: ASR for SafeQwen2.5-VL-32B (it shows clean consistency 100 but no refusal-rate result), and ASR values for DeepSeek-VL2 and Qwen3-VL, which the text says have no refusals
Which intervention (subtraction vs. ablation) produced the reported ASR, and the per-seed success rate rather than best-of-five
Per-model degeneration rates and the chosen α, which separate refusal failures from invalid outputs

record.verdict_notes: The study primarily measures demographic bias; refusal removal is the means. ASR is best-of-five seed directions at a per-model chosen layer and α, which inflates removal rates relative to a single fixed direction. Table D.1 text extraction is ambiguous for the Gemma-4 and Qwen3.6 columns. The cosine-similarity drop at the intervention layer (Fig. B.1) is not a refusal rate.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test adding the direction, removing it from every layer and position, or preservation of general capabilities. It tests refusal suppression on V-SBB visual demographic-selection queries, using a calibrated intervention layer.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is evaluated.
No test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
No comparison of a single direction with an affine, conic, or multi-direction account.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision is tested.
No direction transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages is tested.
No variation or comparison of refusal-training procedures or timing.

relation.reason: Table 1 gives the rate of the behaviour (valid answer instead of refusal) under direction steering vs no intervention, for three refusing models. Only removal is tested. Induction and capability retention are not tested.

tranche.reason: It applies an Arditi-style difference-in-means direction, adapted to paired text-image inputs, in a new setting (VLMs on image-based demographic selection queries). It reports refusal-suppression ASR against an unsteered Clean baseline, which is a result on V1's removal part. Bias measurement is the main aim, but the removal rates are reported per model.

source_check.notes: The pack listed no [lN] ids, so l1 and l2 are numbered in pack order. Table 1 does not separate subtraction from ablation. ASR failures include invalid or degenerate output, so ASR is a lower bound on refusal removal. Table D.1 answer consistency is Gemma-4 77.6, Qwen3.6 56.8 and Llama-3.2-Vision 45.9, so steering changes many answers the model already gave. The main text says SBB 'consistently' scores lower, but Table 1 has Llama at 87.6 for SBB vs 85.3. The V1.support[4] material attributed to this study probably comes from another paper.

statements.correction: 8FVZVYg5nD: the direction is a difference in means, harmful minus harmless (Arditi splits, 128 each), with each prompt paired with a random benchmark image. No SVD. Only removal is tested (subtraction or ablation at one selected layer, α in {1,2,3}). No addition on safe or harmless inputs, no Qwen2.5-VL-7B, no random, negative or orthogonal control, no code link and no uncertainty. Its Llama-3.2-11B-Vision-Instruct result is removal: ASR 13.0→85.3 (Table 1).
statements.problem: Misattributed to this study: an SVD direction of refused-unsafe vs safe text, adding the direction to induce refusal, the Qwen2.5-VL-7B 92% and Llama-3.2-11B-Vision 82% results, -d̂ and orthogonal controls, and 'code y, controls y'. None of these is in this text, and rows R7-R12 are not this record's row ids (r1-r9). The pack header gives code: n.

None for this study. Gemma-4-31B-it 32.6→89.7 and Llama-3.2-11B-Vision 13.0→85.3 are in Table 1. Best-of-five seed directions and ASR counting invalid output as failure match Section 5.1. The listed layers (12, 27) and direction types (GEVD, readouts, text-derived) belong to other studies.
